title.narrative: Inclusive and Protective Education in Emergency Response for Conflict-Affected Children in North Shoa Zone of Amhara region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project will address critical humanitarian needs of 5842 children by delivering education in emergency settings, ensuring access to inclusive and protective learning environments in active conflict zones of Amhara and North Shewa zone, Eferatana woreda. Focused interventions will target areas where ongoing conflicts have resulted in widespread school closures. In North Shewa zone, Eferatana woreda, while a higher percentage of schools are open, 43% still remain closed, depriving 9,410 children of education for the past two years.ltbrgtThe project is strategically designed to restore access to safe, inclusive, and adaptable learning opportunities while fortifying local systems and engaging communities to sustain education in emergencies. Central to its mission is fostering the psychosocial resilience and well-being of children in the crisis-affected areas. In response to the non-operational status of schools in the areas, the project will pioneer a novel approach by bringing learning directly to children's homes through a blended education model. This innovative method involves establishing cluster learning centers or groups in close proximity to children's residences, within 200-500 meters, and delivering home-based instruction through a variety of activities conducted in these centers and at children homes. Rather than constructing new facilities, the intervention will utilize existing community spaces—such as churches, mosques, community halls, and safe communal areas—thereby reducing cost, enhancing community ownership, and enabling rapid implementation. ltbrgtThe established learning centers will be utilized to deliver inclusive, non-formal education to out-of-school children aged 7–14. For ages 7–9, sessions will focus on foundational literacy and numeracy, integrated with psychosocial support to build both academic and emotional resilience. Using a slightly contextualized version of our PlayMatters home-based learning package, these younger learners will be engaged through structured, child-friendly content. For older children aged 10–14, the project will implement the Accelerated Education Program (AEP), in line with Ethiopian education policy, which mandates AEP for children out of school for over two years at this age. Targeting this age group (7-14) is a strategic and high-impact investment, as they are developmentally ready for rapid learning and reintegration into formal education systems. To strengthen learning outcomes and ensure continuity, the AEP will be complemented by Radio Education Program interventions. These broadcasts will extend academic support beyond the classroom, reinforcing key competencies and reaching children in remote or underserved areas. ltbrgtThis project is 100% focused on education, targeting out-of-school children through the provision of quality, inclusive, and accelerated learning opportunities. While the core of the intervention is firmly rooted in education, the project will systematically integrate cross-cutting child protection components—particularly Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and Social Emotional Learning (SEL) as essential enablers of safe and effective learning. These elements will be embedded within teacher training, classroom instruction, and the overall learning environment to ensure that children not only access education but are also supported to heal, thrive, and remain engaged. ltbrgtlt/pgt
